changes: Chronogram re-read: viśi(kh)a=5, yuga=4, śara=5, read right to left = NS 545 (cataloguer correct); removed the first reading's unfounded emendation to NS 745; ce_approx 1625 -> 1425

date.as_written: śrīmannepālavarṣe viśiṣayugaśare phālguṇe māsakṛṣṇe pañcamyāḥ anvabādhe'śvaragurusvadine vajrayoge

notes: Chronogram 'viśiṣayugaśare' = viśikha (arrow, 5) + yuga (4) + śara (5), read right to left = NS 545 (1424/25 CE), as the catalogue says. 'viśiṣa' is a slip for viśikha. The colophon falls into two parts. The first (verse colophon with the NS 545 date and the scribe Rāmagupta) cannot belong to the reign of Jagajjyotirmalla (Bhaktapur, c. NS 733-757 / 1613-1637 CE), who is named in the second part (fol. 41r-41v) together with the mahāmātras Rājasiṃhadeva and Nāthasiṃhadeva ('etayoḥ śirobhūtaprastāvakṣaṇe'). The likeliest explanation is that the NS 545 colophon of the exemplar was copied over, and that the present Maithili copy was made under Jagajjyotirmalla (c. 1613-1637). In that case Rāmagupta is the scribe of the exemplar, not of this copy, and the scribe of this copy is unnamed. A miscomputed chronogram is less likely. 'anvabādhe'śvaragurusvadine' is corrupt: 'guru' gives Thursday. 'gobhāmadāyāḥ' in the praise of the scribe is unclear and possibly corrupt (a mother's name or a place?). It is left unidentified. The -deva of the two mahāmātras may be honorific rather than part of their names.
